pr_body:
Hey @pleerock, so I tried to implement #718. It works up to the point where the [raw result is transformed into an entity](https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/master/src/query-builder/SelectQueryBuilder.ts#L1557). Since the result does not have all the relevant columns, it is not converted into an entity. I'm not sure exactly how to handle that. Thoughts?

Fixes #718
pr_comments:
to make transformation working it needs entity id (ids). We have two choices here:

* select entity id/ids during in sql query even if user didn't included them in "select" FORCLY. It means result data will always have ids which may be confusing for users

* try to select entity id/ids during in sql query but do not write it into the entity. This should work much better but implementation is a bit more complex.

Second way is preferable, are you able to implement it?

I would like to implement the second one. However, I'm not sure why but the select I added is not aliasing the columns. It generates the sql **SELECT name, description FROM "photo" "Photo** instead of **SELECT `Photo`.`name` AS `Photo_name`, `Photo`.`description` AS `Photo_description` FROM `photo` `Photo`**. I've tried looking everywhere, and I can't seem to find out where that's happening. It's relevant because the aliased columns are [assumed](https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/master/src/query-builder/transformer/RawSqlResultsToEntityTransformer.ts#L52) when doing the transform.

ah I know why. You need to select using main alias. Append it. In query builder we do:

```ts
createQueryBuilder("post")
.select("post.name")
.addSelect("post.description")
...
```

Same must be done there - apply main alias before each select user does
I made commit that should fix it, please check that

Thanks! That's exactly what I needed. 

So, I found a way to handle the partial results, but it seems a little hacky to me. It's the simplest one I could think of though. Keeping track of the id and removing it from the entity seemed like it would be more complex. Let me know what you think of everything

I don't think its possible to implement it and have a correct behaviour without selecting entity id. You need to write a more complex test with lot of data (lets say 10 posts and each post has 5 categories). Create `name` column in both post and category and partial select it. And you'll need to make partial loading of post with non partial loaded category (e.g. full category) and load partial post with partial category data.

I think you need to load entity id even user didnt specified them (check in createSelectExpression if entity primary columns are not specified and them if so, maybe with "virtual" flag or some other criteria we need to determine that we should not put it into destination entity). In goruping we still use entity id, but we simply don't write entity id into final entity

Okay, the tricky thing though is how to pass the data around. There's no access to EntityMetadata in the SelectQueryBuilder which would have been useful. Passing the metadata into the FindOptionUtils various apply methods generates too many changes.

I ended up adding virtual selects that are removed after transforming the raw results. I think EntityManager needs a little refactoring though. I had to duplicate a lot there. Also, this way involved passing metadata into FindOptionUtils methods like I mentioned. If you have a better suggestion, I would like to know. 

Also, I rewrote the tests with more data. Let me know if something is not done right or missing
Can you rerun the travis build? Only the `node: 6` failed, and it doesn't even seem related
This is a great feature. Will it be on the next release?
Thank you very much for this PR. I merged it and made small fixes we were talking about in above commit. This feature will be released in `0.1.0-alpha.36`. And sorry for being rude again 😆

Next step for this feature is to:

* add tests for partial selection using query builder instead of find options and make sure ids are automatically selected and they arent stored in entity
* add tests with partial selection of columns inside embed entities
* add tests with partial selection and not selected ids inside embed entity
* add tests for partial selection of joined entities

If you have time and want to contribute feel free please :)
Correct. Primary keys are very important and lot of operations inside ORM are based on them. So if you don't want to get benefits of orm make partial selections and take a raw sql results instead

issue_context.title: Question: would it be valid to implement an extra option on find/findOne methods?
issue_context.body:
I mean, currently I have to use query builder to select just a few columns from my table, using the find methods on a specific repository returns all columns.

I think it would be nice to have a key on "options" for specifying the columns that I wish to select. 

Any thoughts?
comments: can you please provide code snippets on what you do right now and how you would like to do

currently if I run 
`const user = await userRepository.findOne({username: 'username'});`, I'll get one user with all the columns that this table has, if I wanted just one column, I would have to do:
```js
const user = await userRepository
     .createQueryBuilder('row')
     .select('row.username')
     .where('row.username = :name', {name: 'username'})
     .getOne();
``` 

and I thought that if I used the options object on `findOne`, I could run something like this: 
`const user = await userRepository.findOne({username: 'username'}, {select: 'username'});`
Hey @pleerock, if no one has picked this up, I would be interested in implementing it

review_comments: I commented out this test because I'm not sure how to handle this case. If we allow virtual primary columns for this case, then the test passes. But it might be unexpected behaviour for users of querybuilder to have ids inserted into their queries when not specified. I think we should only use the virtual columns when coming from the repository

I couldn't figure out a way to differentiate this select and the regular ones that are done with the query builder. Using virtual columns makes other query builder tests to break because a primary column is inserted into the sql. I don't like this, and I'm hoping you can think of something better.

> because a primary column is inserted into the sql

you need to insert primary columns only if they aren't selected at all (if something is selected, but not primary columns). You don't need this ugly flag. Try to redesign this thing

If you check, that's exactly what I'm doing. I'm only selecting the primary columns if they have not already been selected. However it's not enough.

Also, you're coming off as a bit rude you know? I have been courteous and willing to listen to every suggestion.
I'm rude? Sorry if I am, I don't want to be so haha. I just wanted to say that this code can be better and must be redesigned (you know it too, right)
Im on vacation until end of month and have limited laptop access. Once I get out of vacation I can checkout your work and figure what we should do to remove this flag

Okay that's good. I know the flag isn't right. I definitely do not want it and would prefer if it is removed. I just wanted to demonstrate the issue to you.

If I only check if there have been selects, it breaks the other query builder tests that check the sql output. I'm willing to wait until you're back from vacation since you have a better understanding of the code. There might be something obvious that would solve this that I've missed. 

Enjoy your holiday.
